# Independently generated hybrid fixture

`hybrid-torrenttools.torrent` was generated by **torrenttools v0.6.2**
(<https://github.com/fbdtemme/torrenttools>, Rust, AppImage
`torrenttools-0.6.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage`), not by this repository's Go
fixture builder and not by anacrolix/torrent. Its metainfo is therefore
independent evidence for the adapter's hybrid handling.

## Recipe

Payload (exact bytes, reproducible with any scripting language):

| file    | length  | content            |
|---------|---------|--------------------|
| `a.bin` | 70000   | `0x61` repeated    |
| `b.bin` | 40000   | `0x62` repeated    |
| `c.bin` | 100000  | `0x63` repeated    |

All three live under a directory named `fixture/`.

```sh
mkdir -p fixture
python3 - <<'PY'
for name, n, ch in [("a.bin", 70000, b"a"), ("b.bin", 40000, b"b"), ("c.bin", 100000, b"c")]:
    open("fixture/" + name, "wb").write(ch * n)
PY
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./torrenttools.AppImage create fixture \
  --protocol hybrid --piece-size 32K --no-creation-date --no-cross-seed \
  -o hybrid-torrenttools.torrent
```

`--no-creation-date` and `--no-cross-seed` keep the output deterministic: the
committed file hashes to
`4938e5f83eb9623634327d6a0e5dc774c2f187af851be342bfc7815bc89122f4`.

## What it contains

```
name=fixture pieceLen=32768 hasV1=true hasV2=true pieces=9 layers=3
v1=94000f5e6663d82938d86ed20c7966a146bb5c41
v2=3b7eb6eb8bfa16dd14b25cdacfa6d8af3f0cdff2ae4a5f3dee3dea72b7e17c1d
file[0] 70000 a.bin    file[1] 40000 b.bin    file[2] 100000 c.bin
```

`a.bin` and `b.bin` end mid-piece, `c.bin` spans four pieces, and the v2 view
stores three piece layers (one per file longer than a piece). The v1 `files`
list is the continuous layout, so **v1 piece boundaries and v2 piece boundaries
differ** — exactly the case a same-code builder can accidentally agree with
itself on.

## What it does not contain

torrenttools v0.6.2 emits **no BEP 47 padding entries** (`attr: p`,
`_padding/...`); it has no flag for them. So this fixture proves independent
hybrid metainfo interoperability, and it does *not* cover protocol padding. The
adapter's padding policy is covered separately by a unit test that constructs a
padding entry directly, and that gap is stated in `docs/TORRENT.md`.

## Reproducing

The generator is not needed by the test suite: the test reads the committed
`.torrent` and writes the payload bytes above into a temp directory for the
loopback seeder. No network access is required at test time.
